items.title: Why Ken Paxton’s Estranged Wife Is Making the Case for His Senate Campaign
items.author: Beth Reinhard and Lisa Lerer
items.content: <article>Angela Paxton is urging Texas voters to support Mr. Paxton’s Senate campaign, even as she is divorcing him and accusing him of adultery. She has political aspirations of her own.</article>

items.title: Beach in Guam: Supreme Court Considers if Military Can Explode Bombs in This Habitat
items.author: Abbie VanSickle and Hiroko Masuike
items.content: <article>The Supreme Court will hear arguments over whether the U.S. Air Force can keep destroying munitions on a beach in Guam, a practice it began in 1982.</article>

items.title: As Race Tightens, Republicans Resume Tepid Support For Max Miller in Ohio
items.author: Emily Davies and Tyler Pager
items.content: <article>The embattled congressman, accused of throwing scalding water at his ex-wife and breaking his daughter’s collarbone, rebuffed earlier Republican calls to drop out.</article>

items.title: Takeaways From the First Maine Senate Debate Between Susan Collins and Troy Jackson
items.author: Lisa Lerer, Tim Balk and Emily Davies
items.content: <article>Senator Susan Collins, one of the most vulnerable Republicans in the midterms, clashed with the Democratic challenger Troy Jackson over President Trump, ICE and more.</article>

items.title: Amid Midterm Crunch, Trump Advisers Took Time to Help Russia-Aligned Government
items.author: Kenneth P. Vogel
items.content: <article>James Blair and Chris LaCivita, who are leading the president’s congressional campaign operation, traveled to Republika Srpska to provide election advice.</article>

items.title: Justice Dept. Turns to Partisans and Conspiracists to Fill Depleted Ranks
items.author: Glenn Thrush
items.content: <article>The civil rights unit has recruited people whose questionable work histories and dearth of education and experience might have disqualified them in the past, former officials said.</article>

items.title: Five Takeaways in New Book From Thom Tillis, Who Turned on Trump
items.author: Annie Karni
items.content: <article>In “How to Lose Friends and Antagonize Presidents,” Senator Thom Tillis details his regrets about backing President Trump’s agenda.</article>

items.title: How a Maryland Shipyard Turned Into a Squabble Between Trump and Wes Moore
items.author: Luke Broadwater
items.content: <article>President Trump traveled to Baltimore to announce a major investment that he said would create new jobs. Gov. Wes Moore of Maryland, a Democrat, says he deserves credit, too.</article>

items.title: In Iceland, Rubio Dodges a Diplomatic Flap Over a Trump Map
items.author: Michael Crowley
items.content: <article>President Trump had posted a map on his Truth Social account in September depicting Iceland as part of U.S. territory.</article>

items.title: Democrats Look Strong in Polls, Thanks to These Voter Groups
items.author: Ruth Igielnik
items.content: <article>Different blocs are moving left. They could swing key Senate races.</article>

items.title: Trump Does Not Plan to Reimburse Taxpayers for Promotional Ads
items.author: Shane Goldmacher and Maggie Haberman
items.content: <article>A day after the president said his super PAC would pay for the ads, which had drawn bipartisan backlash, officials said that he meant moving forward. A new taxpayer-funded ad aired Tuesday.</article>

items.title: Wrongly Indicted Man Seeks Inquiry of Official Conduct in Reflecting Pool Case
items.author: Devlin Barrett
items.content: <article>Lawyers for the former Olympian David Hearn accused prosecutors of ignoring their own evidence to indict him and then providing “blatantly false” information about what they knew when.</article>

items.title: An Influential Voice in the Climate Debate Has Died at 66
items.author: Clay Risen
items.content: <article>Joe Romm was a prolific writer who never hesitated to take on climate change deniers and the fossil-fuel industry — or even ostensible allies.</article>

items.title: Ex-C.I.A. Officer Who Stashed Gold Bars Admits to Far Larger $145 Million Scam
items.author: Devlin Barrett
items.content: <article>A plea hearing revealed a far larger pattern of fraud against the government, while keeping some key secrets still hidden.</article>

items.title: What, Exactly, Did Trump Say About Iran Taking Out Los Angeles and San Diego?
items.author: Shawn McCreesh
items.content: <article>President Trump’s comments caused an uproar from members of both parties. A White House official said he was taken out of context.</article>

items.title: Republicans are spending to aid Darline Graham as the South Carolina Senate race tightens.
items.author: Emily Davies
items.content: <article>Senator Darline Graham, Republican of South Carolina, during a Senate committee hearing on Capitol Hill last month.</article>

items.title: Short on Cash, Democrats Weigh Big Bets to Unseat Entrenched Republicans
items.author: Shane Goldmacher
items.content: <article>With less money than G.O.P., Democrats are torn over where to spend in the final weeks. The party is making its biggest move in years against one of G.O.P.’s biggest blue-district survivors.</article>

items.title: Top Super PAC for Senate Democrats Raises Record $151 Million in Third Quarter
items.author: Shane Goldmacher
items.content: <article>Democratic Senate candidates have generally out-raised Republicans, but are struggling to match outside spending from Trump-affiliated groups.</article>

items.title: Man Arrested in Connection With Incident at UK Air Base RAF Fairford
items.author: Megan Specia
items.content: <article>A 22-year-old from London was the seventh person to be arrested by the counterterrorism police investigating an incident at R.A.F. Fairford last month.</article>
